title: Times Table Painter
story: The school wall needs times tables painted. Print one for any number.
goal: Read n. Print n x 1 = ... through n x 10 = ..., one per line, like: 3 x 1 = 3
starter:
n = int(input())
# print the table for n, 1 to 10
hints: Use for i in range(...) and decide which numbers you need: 1 to 10 inclusive.
range(1, 11) gives 1..10. Print an f-string inside the loop.
socratic: What stays the same each round, and what changes?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the key idea in “Times Table Painter”?
alt:
n = int(input())
i = 1
while i <= 10:
    print(str(n) + " x " + str(i) + " = " + str(n * i))
    i += 1

example.title: Worked example: squares
example.code:
for i in range(1, 4):
    print(i, "squared is", i * i)
example.note: Use the loop variable inside the print to make each line different.
